// Every error the public API returns, one test per function.

use musicrs::{MusicError, MusicEstimator, select_bins_by_energy, stft};
use nalgebra::DMatrix;
use num_complex::Complex;
use std::f64::consts::PI;

const NFFT: usize = 160;

/// A 1 kHz tone, the same on all four Kinect microphones.
fn tone(n_samples: usize) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    DMatrix::from_fn(4, n_samples, |m, t| {
        (2.0 * PI * 1000.0 * t as f64 / 16000.0 + m as f64).cos()
    })
}

fn with_nan(mut data: DMatrix<f64>) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    data[(2, 10)] = f64::NAN;
    data
}

const TOO_MANY: MusicError = MusicError::TooManySources {
    n_sources: 4,
    n_antennas: 4,
};

#[test]
fn estimate_doa_from_real_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let doa = |data: &DMatrix<f64>, n_sources| est.estimate_doa_from_real(data, n_sources, 1000.0);
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&DMatrix::zeros(3, 100), 1),
        Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
            expected: 4,
            got: 3
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(doa(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 0), 1), Err(MusicError::EmptyData));
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&with_nan(tone(1000)), 1),
        Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData)
    );
    let mut inf = tone(1000);
    inf[(0, 0)] = f64::INFINITY;
    assert_eq!(doa(&inf, 1), Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData));
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 1000), 1),
        Err(MusicError::SilentData)
    );
    // A constant offset is removed with the mean, leaving silence
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&DMatrix::from_element(4, 1000, 0.3), 1),
        Err(MusicError::SilentData)
    );
    assert_eq!(doa(&tone(1000), 4), Err(TOO_MANY));
}

#[test]
fn estimate_doa_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let doa = |data: &DMatrix<Complex<f64>>| est.estimate_doa(data, 1, 1000.0);
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&DMatrix::from_element(3, 100, Complex::new(1.0, 0.5))),
        Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
            expected: 4,
            got: 3
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(doa(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 0)), Err(MusicError::EmptyData));
    let mut nan = DMatrix::from_element(4, 100, Complex::new(1.0, 0.5));
    nan[(1, 1)] = Complex::new(0.0, f64::NAN);
    assert_eq!(doa(&nan), Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData));
    assert_eq!(doa(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 100)), Err(MusicError::SilentData));
}

#[test]
fn noise_subspace_and_spectrum_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for (rows, cols) in [(3, 3), (4, 3), (3, 4)] {
        assert_eq!(
            est.noise_subspace(&DMatrix::identity(rows, cols), 1),
            Err(MusicError::CovarianceShape {
                n_antennas: 4,
                rows,
                cols
            })
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(
        est.noise_subspace(&DMatrix::identity(4, 3), 1)
            .unwrap_err()
            .to_string(),
        "covariance matrix is 4 × 3, expected 4 × 4 (one row and column per antenna)"
    );
    let mut nan = DMatrix::identity(4, 4);
    nan[(0, 1)] = Complex::new(f64::NAN, 0.0);
    assert_eq!(est.noise_subspace(&nan, 1), Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData));
    assert_eq!(
        est.noise_subspace(&DMatrix::identity(4, 4), 4),
        Err(TOO_MANY)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        est.spectrum(&DMatrix::identity(3, 2), 1000.0),
        Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
            expected: 4,
            got: 3
        })
    );
}

/// Constant data is silent once its mean is removed, whatever the constant and length:
/// the rounding residue stays below the silence threshold.
#[test]
fn constant_data_is_silent() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for c in [0.3, -0.1, 1.0 / 3.0, PI * 1e5, 1e6 + 0.3, 7e-9, 1e12 / 7.0] {
        for n in [2, 3, 1000, 1601, 16000] {
            let data = DMatrix::from_element(4, n, c);
            assert_eq!(
                est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0),
                Err(MusicError::SilentData),
                "c = {c}, n = {n}"
            );
            if n >= NFFT {
                assert_eq!(
                    est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, None),
                    Err(MusicError::SilentData),
                    "IFB: c = {c}, n = {n}"
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

/// An unusable angle grid is an error wherever the grid is searched. `new` does not check
/// it, because the fields are public and can change after construction.
#[test]
fn invalid_angle_grid_errors() {
    let data = tone(1024);
    let n = MusicEstimator::default().n_antennas();
    for (steps, interval) in [
        (0, (0.0, PI)),
        (360, (PI, 0.0)),
        (360, (1.0, 1.0)),
        (360, (0.0, f64::NAN)),
        (360, (f64::NEG_INFINITY, 0.0)),
    ] {
        let est = MusicEstimator::new(
            MusicEstimator::default().antenna_positions,
            steps,
            interval,
            16000.0,
        );
        let is_grid_err = |e: MusicError| matches!(e, MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid { .. });
        assert!(is_grid_err(
            est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0).unwrap_err()
        ));
        assert!(is_grid_err(
            est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, None).unwrap_err()
        ));
        assert!(is_grid_err(
            est.spectrum(&DMatrix::identity(n, n - 1), 1000.0)
                .unwrap_err()
        ));
    }
}

    };
    assert!(shifted.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0).is_ok());
}

/// The signal frequency must be finite and positive, for every function that takes one.
#[test]
fn invalid_frequency_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let data = tone(1600);
    let complex = data.map(|x| Complex::new(x, 0.0));
    for freq in [0.0, -1000.0, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY] {
        let expected = Err(MusicError::InvalidFrequency(freq));
        assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, freq), expected);
        assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa(&complex, 1, freq), expected);
        assert_eq!(
            est.spectrum(&DMatrix::identity(4, 3), freq).map(|_| ()),
            expected.map(|_| ())
        );
    }
    assert!(matches!(
        est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, f64::NAN),
        Err(MusicError::InvalidFrequency(f)) if f.is_nan()
    ));
}

/// IFB never uses the DC bin: it has no direction information.
#[test]
fn ifb_music_spectrum_ignores_dc_bin() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let data = tone(1600).map(|x| x + 0.5);
    assert_eq!(
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[0]))
            .map(|_| ()),
        Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[0, 10])),
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[10]))
    );
}

/// The complex entry point checks the source count and the angle grid itself.
#[test]
fn estimate_doa_parameter_errors() {
    let complex = tone(1000).map(|x| Complex::new(x, 0.0));
    assert_eq!(
        MusicEstimator::default().estimate_doa(&complex, 4, 1000.0),
        Err(TOO_MANY)
    );
    let no_grid = MusicEstimator {
        angle_steps_num: 0,
        ..MusicEstimator::default()
    };
    assert!(matches!(
        no_grid.estimate_doa(&complex, 1, 1000.0),
        Err(MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid { .. })
    ));
}

/// An estimator without antennas has room for no source.
#[test]
fn no_antennas() {
    let est = MusicEstimator {
        antenna_positions: vec![],
        ..MusicEstimator::default()
    };
    let none = |n_sources| MusicError::TooManySources {
        n_sources,
        n_antennas: 0,
    };
    let data = DMatrix::zeros(0, 1000);
    assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 0, 1000.0), Err(none(0)));
    assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0), Err(none(1)));
    assert_eq!(
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 0, None).map(|_| ()),
        Err(none(0))
    );
    assert_eq!(
        none(0).to_string(),
        "0 sources requested, but at most 0 fit 0 antennas"
    );
}

/// A noise subspace that annihilates every steering vector (all zeros, or no columns)
/// scores every angle as infinitely likely, instead of dividing by zero into NaN.
#[test]
fn spectrum_of_zero_noise_subspace_is_infinite() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for noise in [DMatrix::zeros(4, 3), DMatrix::zeros(4, 0)] {
        let (spectrum, angles) = est.spectrum(&noise, 1000.0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(angles.len(), 720);
        assert!(spectrum.iter().all(|&s| s == f64::INFINITY));
    }
}

//! Errors returned by the musicrs API.

use std::fmt;

/// Why a musicrs function could not produce a result.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum MusicError {
    /// The data (or noise subspace) has the wrong number of rows: one per antenna is
    /// expected.
    RowCountMismatch { expected: usize, got: usize },
    /// The covariance matrix is not `n_antennas × n_antennas`.
    CovarianceShape {
        n_antennas: usize,
        rows: usize,
        cols: usize,
    },
    /// The data has no rows or no samples.
    EmptyData,
    /// The data is shorter than one STFT window, so it has no complete window.
    DataShorterThanWindow { nfft: usize, samples: usize },
    /// The data contains a NaN or infinite value.
    NonFiniteData,
    /// The data (after removing each channel's mean, for real data) is all zeros, or
    /// every selected frequency bin is: there is no signal to locate.
    SilentData,
    /// `n_sources` must be less than the number of antennas, so that a noise subspace
    /// is left.
    TooManySources { n_sources: usize, n_antennas: usize },
    /// The STFT window size `nfft` is 0.
    InvalidNfft,
    /// The STFT overlap must be less than the window size.
    InvalidOverlap { no_overlap: usize, nfft: usize },
    /// The bin-selection threshold must be finite and non-negative.
    InvalidThreshold(f64),
    /// None of the requested frequency bins is usable: each must be in `1..=nfft / 2`
    /// (the DC bin 0 has no direction information).
    NoUsableBins,
    /// The angle grid is unusable: `angle_steps_num` must be positive and the search
    /// interval finite with `start < end`, spanning at most 2π (a wider one visits some
    /// directions twice).
    InvalidAngleGrid {
        angle_steps_num: usize,
        search_interval: (f64, f64),
    },
    /// The signal frequency must be finite and positive: at 0 Hz every direction scores
    /// the same.
    InvalidFrequency(f64),
    /// The estimator's `sample_rate` must be finite and positive.
    InvalidSampleRate(f64),
    /// An antenna position (the antenna at `index`) is NaN or infinite.
    InvalidAntennaPosition { index: usize },
}

impl fmt::Display for MusicError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::RowCountMismatch { expected, got } => {
                write!(f, "expected {expected} rows (one per antenna), got {got}")
            }
            Self::CovarianceShape {
                n_antennas,
                rows,
                cols,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "covariance matrix is {rows} × {cols}, expected {n_antennas} × {n_antennas} \
                 (one row and column per antenna)"
            ),
            Self::EmptyData => write!(f, "data has no samples"),
            Self::DataShorterThanWindow { nfft, samples } => write!(
                f,
                "data has {samples} samples, fewer than one STFT window of {nfft}"
            ),
            Self::NonFiniteData => write!(f, "data contains NaN or infinite values"),
            Self::SilentData => write!(f, "data is silent: there is no signal to locate"),
            Self::TooManySources {
                n_sources,
                n_antennas,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "{n_sources} sources requested, but at most {} fit {n_antennas} antennas",
                n_antennas.saturating_sub(1)
            ),
            Self::InvalidNfft => write!(f, "nfft must be at least 1"),
            Self::InvalidOverlap { no_overlap, nfft } => write!(
                f,
                "overlap of {no_overlap} samples must be less than nfft = {nfft}"
            ),
            Self::InvalidThreshold(t) => {
                write!(f, "threshold must be finite and non-negative, got {t} dB")
            }
            Self::NoUsableBins => write!(
                f,
                "none of the requested frequency bins is usable (each must be in 1..=nfft/2)"
            ),
            Self::InvalidAngleGrid {
                angle_steps_num,
                search_interval: (start, end),
            } => write!(
                f,
                "invalid angle grid: {angle_steps_num} steps over ({start}, {end}); \
                 need at least one step and a finite interval with start < end spanning at most 2π"
            ),
            Self::InvalidFrequency(freq) => {
                write!(f, "frequency must be finite and positive, got {freq} Hz")
            }
            Self::InvalidSampleRate(sr) => {
                write!(f, "sample rate must be finite and positive, got {sr} Hz")
            }
            Self::InvalidAntennaPosition { index } => {
                write!(f, "antenna {index} has a NaN or infinite position")
            }
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for MusicError {}

/// `Result` with [`MusicError`] as the error type. It is not re-exported at the crate
/// root, so that `use musicrs::*` does not shadow `std::result::Result`.
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, MusicError>;

// Every error the public API returns, one test per function.

use musicrs::{MusicError, MusicEstimator, select_bins_by_energy, stft};
use nalgebra::DMatrix;
use num_complex::Complex;
use std::f64::consts::PI;

const NFFT: usize = 160;

/// A 1 kHz tone, the same on all four Kinect microphones.
fn tone(n_samples: usize) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    DMatrix::from_fn(4, n_samples, |m, t| {
        (2.0 * PI * 1000.0 * t as f64 / 16000.0 + m as f64).cos()
    })
}

fn with_nan(mut data: DMatrix<f64>) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    data[(2, 10)] = f64::NAN;
    data
}

const TOO_MANY: MusicError = MusicError::TooManySources {
    n_sources: 4,
    n_antennas: 4,
};

#[test]
fn estimate_doa_from_real_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let doa = |data: &DMatrix<f64>, n_sources| est.estimate_doa_from_real(data, n_sources, 1000.0);
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&DMatrix::zeros(3, 100), 1),
        Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
            expected: 4,
            got: 3
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(doa(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 0), 1), Err(MusicError::EmptyData));
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&with_nan(tone(1000)), 1),
        Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData)
    );
    let mut inf = tone(1000);
    inf[(0, 0)] = f64::INFINITY;
    assert_eq!(doa(&inf, 1), Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData));
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 1000), 1),
        Err(MusicError::SilentData)
    );
    // A constant offset is removed with the mean, leaving silence
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&DMatrix::from_element(4, 1000, 0.3), 1),
        Err(MusicError::SilentData)
    );
    assert_eq!(doa(&tone(1000), 4), Err(TOO_MANY));
}

#[test]
fn estimate_doa_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let doa = |data: &DMatrix<Complex<f64>>| est.estimate_doa(data, 1, 1000.0);
    assert_eq!(
        doa(&DMatrix::from_element(3, 100, Complex::new(1.0, 0.5))),
        Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
            expected: 4,
            got: 3
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(doa(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 0)), Err(MusicError::EmptyData));
    let mut nan = DMatrix::from_element(4, 100, Complex::new(1.0, 0.5));
    nan[(1, 1)] = Complex::new(0.0, f64::NAN);
    assert_eq!(doa(&nan), Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData));
    assert_eq!(doa(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 100)), Err(MusicError::SilentData));
}

#[test]
fn noise_subspace_and_spectrum_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for (rows, cols) in [(3, 3), (4, 3), (3, 4)] {
        assert_eq!(
            est.noise_subspace(&DMatrix::identity(rows, cols), 1),
            Err(MusicError::CovarianceShape {
                n_antennas: 4,
                rows,
                cols
            })
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(
        est.noise_subspace(&DMatrix::identity(4, 3), 1)
            .unwrap_err()
            .to_string(),
        "covariance matrix is 4 × 3, expected 4 × 4 (one row and column per antenna)"
    );
    let mut nan = DMatrix::identity(4, 4);
    nan[(0, 1)] = Complex::new(f64::NAN, 0.0);
    assert_eq!(est.noise_subspace(&nan, 1), Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData));
    assert_eq!(
        est.noise_subspace(&DMatrix::identity(4, 4), 4),
        Err(TOO_MANY)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        est.spectrum(&DMatrix::identity(3, 2), 1000.0),
        Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
            expected: 4,
            got: 3
        })
    );
}

/// Constant data is silent once its mean is removed, whatever the constant and length:
/// the rounding residue stays below the silence threshold.
#[test]
fn constant_data_is_silent() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for c in [0.3, -0.1, 1.0 / 3.0, PI * 1e5, 1e6 + 0.3, 7e-9, 1e12 / 7.0] {
        for n in [2, 3, 1000, 1601, 16000] {
            let data = DMatrix::from_element(4, n, c);
            assert_eq!(
                est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0),
                Err(MusicError::SilentData),
                "c = {c}, n = {n}"
            );
            if n >= NFFT {
                assert_eq!(
                    est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, None),
                    Err(MusicError::SilentData),
                    "IFB: c = {c}, n = {n}"
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

/// An unusable angle grid is an error wherever the grid is searched. `new` does not check
/// it, because the fields are public and can change after construction.
#[test]
fn invalid_angle_grid_errors() {
    let data = tone(1024);
    let n = MusicEstimator::default().n_antennas();
    for (steps, interval) in [
        (0, (0.0, PI)),
        (360, (PI, 0.0)),
        (360, (1.0, 1.0)),
        (360, (0.0, f64::NAN)),
        (360, (f64::NEG_INFINITY, 0.0)),
    ] {
        let est = MusicEstimator::new(
            MusicEstimator::default().antenna_positions,
            steps,
            interval,
            16000.0,
        );
        let is_grid_err = |e: MusicError| matches!(e, MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid { .. });
        assert!(is_grid_err(
            est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0).unwrap_err()
        ));
        assert!(is_grid_err(
            est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, None).unwrap_err()
        ));
        assert!(is_grid_err(
            est.spectrum(&DMatrix::identity(n, n - 1), 1000.0)
                .unwrap_err()
        ));
    }
}

#[test]
fn ifb_music_spectrum_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let data = tone(1600);
    let ifb = |data: &DMatrix<f64>, nfft, n_sources, bins: Option<&[usize]>| {
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(data, nfft, n_sources, bins)
            .map(|_| ())
    };
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&DMatrix::zeros(3, 1600), NFFT, 1, None),
        Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
            expected: 4,
            got: 3
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&DMatrix::zeros(0, 1600), NFFT, 1, None),
        Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
            expected: 4,
            got: 0
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 0), NFFT, 1, None),
        Err(MusicError::EmptyData)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&with_nan(data.clone()), NFFT, 1, None),
        Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData)
    );
    assert_eq!(ifb(&data, NFFT, 4, None), Err(TOO_MANY));
    assert_eq!(ifb(&data, 0, 1, None), Err(MusicError::InvalidNfft));
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&tone(NFFT - 1), NFFT, 1, None),
        Err(MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow {
            nfft: NFFT,
            samples: NFFT - 1
        })
    );
    // nfft = 1 has only the DC bin, which `None` skips
    assert_eq!(ifb(&data, 1, 1, None), Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins));
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[])),
        Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[NFFT / 2 + 1, 10_000])),
        Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&DMatrix::zeros(4, 1600), NFFT, 1, None),
        Err(MusicError::SilentData)
    );
    // The tone is bin 10; bin 30 holds no power
    assert_eq!(
        ifb(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[30])),
        Err(MusicError::SilentData)
    );
}

/// Bins without power are skipped rather than mixed into the geometric mean.
#[test]
fn ifb_music_spectrum_skips_silent_bins() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let data = tone(1600);
    let (only, _) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[10])).unwrap();
    let (with_silent, _) = est
        .ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[10, 30, 50]))
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(only, with_silent);
}

/// The estimator's own fields are checked where they are used: the sample rate and
/// antenna positions by every function that builds steering vectors.
#[test]
fn invalid_estimator_errors() {
    let data = tone(1600);
    let noise = DMatrix::identity(4, 3);
    let check = |est: &MusicEstimator, expected: MusicError| {
        assert_eq!(
            est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0),
            Err(expected.clone())
        );
        let complex = data.map(|x| Complex::new(x, 0.0));
        assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa(&complex, 1, 1000.0), Err(expected.clone()));
        assert_eq!(
            est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, None).map(|_| ()),
            Err(expected.clone())
        );
        assert_eq!(est.spectrum(&noise, 1000.0).map(|_| ()), Err(expected));
    };
    for sr in [0.0, -16000.0, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY] {
        let est = MusicEstimator {
            sample_rate: sr,
            ..MusicEstimator::default()
        };
        // NaN != NaN, so compare the error's text for it
        if sr.is_nan() {
            assert_eq!(
                est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0)
                    .unwrap_err()
                    .to_string(),
                "sample rate must be finite and positive, got NaN Hz"
            );
        } else {
            check(&est, MusicError::InvalidSampleRate(sr));
        }
    }
    for bad in [f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY] {
        let mut est = MusicEstimator::default();
        est.antenna_positions[2][1] = bad;
        check(&est, MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition { index: 2 });
    }
    // A search interval wider than 2π visits directions twice; exactly 2π is fine
    let wide = MusicEstimator {
        search_interval: (0.0, 4.0 * PI),
        angle_steps_num: 1440,
        ..MusicEstimator::default()
    };
    check(
        &wide,
        MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid {
            angle_steps_num: 1440,
            search_interval: (0.0, 4.0 * PI),
        },
    );
    let shifted = MusicEstimator {
        search_interval: (-PI, PI),
        ..MusicEstimator::default()
    };
    assert!(shifted.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0).is_ok());
}

/// The signal frequency must be finite and positive, for every function that takes one.
#[test]
fn invalid_frequency_errors() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let data = tone(1600);
    let complex = data.map(|x| Complex::new(x, 0.0));
    for freq in [0.0, -1000.0, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY] {
        let expected = Err(MusicError::InvalidFrequency(freq));
        assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, freq), expected);
        assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa(&complex, 1, freq), expected);
        assert_eq!(
            est.spectrum(&DMatrix::identity(4, 3), freq).map(|_| ()),
            expected.map(|_| ())
        );
    }
    assert!(matches!(
        est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, f64::NAN),
        Err(MusicError::InvalidFrequency(f)) if f.is_nan()
    ));
}

#[test]
fn ifb_music_spectrum_ignores_dc_bin() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let data = tone(1600).map(|x| x + 0.5);
    assert_eq!(
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[0]))
            .map(|_| ()),
        Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[0, 10])),
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[10]))

}

#[test]
fn estimate_doa_parameter_errors() {
    let complex = tone(1000).map(|x| Complex::new(x, 0.0));
    assert_eq!(
        MusicEstimator::default().estimate_doa(&complex, 4, 1000.0),
        Err(TOO_MANY)
    );
    let no_grid = MusicEstimator {
        angle_steps_num: 0,
        ..MusicEstimator::default()
    };
    assert!(matches!(
        no_grid.estimate_doa(&complex, 1, 1000.0),
        Err(MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid { .. })
    ));
}

#[test]
fn no_antennas() {
    let est = MusicEstimator {
        antenna_positions: vec![],
        ..MusicEstimator::default()
    };
    let none = |n_sources| MusicError::TooManySources {
        n_sources,
        n_antennas: 0,
    };
    let data = DMatrix::zeros(0, 1000);
    assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 0, 1000.0), Err(none(0)));
    assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0), Err(none(1)));
    assert_eq!(
        est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 0, None).map(|_| ()),
        Err(none(0))
    );
    assert_eq!(
        none(0).to_string(),
        "0 sources requested, but at most 0 fit 0 antennas"
    );
}

/// scores every angle as infinitely likely, instead of dividing by zero into NaN.
#[test]
fn spectrum_of_zero_noise_subspace_is_infinite() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for noise in [DMatrix::zeros(4, 3), DMatrix::zeros(4, 0)] {
        let (spectrum, angles) = est.spectrum(&noise, 1000.0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(angles.len(), 720);
        assert!(spectrum.iter().all(|&s| s == f64::INFINITY));

fn every_error_message() {
    let cases = [

///
/// A tone between two bins leaks into its neighbours, and each selected bin is steered at
/// the bin's frequency rather than the tone's. The mismatch shifts the estimate, most
/// near endfire (0° / 180° for a line array): on the test recordings at `nfft = 1024`
/// (15.6 Hz bins), a single tone is off by up to 5.5° at 0° and 1.5° elsewhere. Choose
/// `nfft` so the tones fall on bins where possible.
///
/// # Errors
/// - [`MusicError::InvalidThreshold`] if `threshold_db` is negative or not finite.
/// - [`MusicError::InvalidNfft`] if `nfft` is 0; [`MusicError::NoUsableBins`] if it is
///   1 (the only bin is DC).
/// - [`MusicError::EmptyData`], [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`] or
///   [`MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow`] for unusable data.
/// - [`MusicError::SilentData`] if every bin except DC has zero power.
///
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// use musicrs::{MusicEstimator, select_bins_by_energy};
/// use nalgebra::DMatrix;
/// use std::f64::consts::PI;
///
/// // A 1 kHz tone: with nfft = 160 at 16 kHz the bins are 100 Hz apart, so it is bin 10.
/// let est = MusicEstimator::default();
/// let data = DMatrix::from_fn(4, 16000, |_, t| (2.0 * PI * 1000.0 * t as f64 / 16000.0).cos());
/// let bins = select_bins_by_energy(&data, 160, 20.0)?;
/// assert_eq!(bins, [10]);
/// let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, 160, 1, Some(&bins))?;
/// # let _ = (spectrum, angles);
/// # Ok::<(), musicrs::MusicError>(())
/// ```
pub fn select_bins_by_energy(
    data: &DMatrix<f64>,
    nfft: usize,
    threshold_db: f64,
) -> Result<Vec<usize>> {
    if !(threshold_db.is_finite() && threshold_db >= 0.0) {
        return Err(MusicError::InvalidThreshold(threshold_db));
    }
    if nfft == 0 {
        return Err(MusicError::InvalidNfft);
    }
    if nfft == 1 {
        return Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins);
    }
    check_real_samples(data)?;
    if data.ncols() < nfft {
        return Err(MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow {
            nfft,
            samples: data.ncols(),
        });
    }
    let mut power = vec![0.0; nfft / 2 + 1];
    for m in 0..data.nrows() {
        let row: Vec<f64> = data.row(m).iter().copied().collect();
        for (p, bin) in power.iter_mut().zip(stft(&row, nfft, 0)?) {
            *p += bin.iter().map(|c| c.norm_sqr()).sum::<f64>() / bin.len() as f64;
        }
    }
    let strongest = power[1..].iter().copied().fold(0.0, f64::max);
    if strongest <= 0.0 {
        return Err(MusicError::SilentData);
    }
    let floor = strongest * 10f64.powf(-threshold_db / 10.0);
    Ok((1..power.len()).filter(|&k| power[k] >= floor).collect())
}

/// A power of two close to `max_abs`, the largest absolute value in some data, to divide
/// the data by. MUSIC does not depend on the data's scale, and dividing by a power of two
/// is exact, so this changes no result: it only keeps the sums of squares in the
/// covariance and energy from overflowing for very loud data (or underflowing for very
/// quiet data).
fn power_of_two_scale(max_abs: f64) -> f64 {
    if max_abs > 0.0 {
        2f64.powi((max_abs.log2().floor() as i32).clamp(-1000, 1000))
    } else {
        1.0
    }
}

/// `data` divided by [`power_of_two_scale`] of its largest absolute value.
fn normalised_real(data: &DMatrix<f64>) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    data / power_of_two_scale(data.amax())
}

/// The mean of `values`, summed with Neumaier's compensated summation so that it is
/// correct to about one ulp: subtracting it from constant data then leaves (almost)
/// nothing, which [`SILENCE_RATIO`] relies on. With a plain sum, 16000 samples of 0.3
/// leave a residue above the threshold.
fn accurate_mean<'a>(values: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a f64>) -> f64 {
    let n = values.len() as f64;
    let (mut sum, mut compensation) = (0.0_f64, 0.0_f64);
    for &x in values {
        let t = sum + x;
        compensation += if sum.abs() >= x.abs() {
            (sum - t) + x
        } else {
            (x - t) + sum
        };
        sum = t;
    }
    (sum + compensation) / n
}

/// Checks that real data has samples and that all of them are finite.
fn check_real_samples(data: &DMatrix<f64>) -> Result<()> {
    if data.is_empty() {
        return Err(MusicError::EmptyData);
    }
    if !data.iter().all(|x| x.is_finite()) {
        return Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData);
    }
    Ok(())
}

    /// Two on-bin tones, the second 6 dB weaker, plus a DC offset stronger than both.
    fn two_tones_with_dc() -> DMatrix<f64> {

            let t = t as f64 / sr;

    nfft: usize,
    threshold_db: f64,

    if !(threshold_db.is_finite() && threshold_db >= 0.0) {
        return Err(MusicError::InvalidThreshold(threshold_db));
    }
    if nfft == 0 {
        return Err(MusicError::InvalidNfft);
    }
    if nfft == 1 {
        return Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins);
    }
    check_real_samples(data)?;
    if data.ncols() < nfft {
        return Err(MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow {
            nfft,
            samples: data.ncols(),
        });
    }
    let mut power = vec![0.0; nfft / 2 + 1];
    for m in 0..data.nrows() {
        let row: Vec<f64> = data.row(m).iter().copied().collect();
        for (p, bin) in power.iter_mut().zip(stft(&row, nfft, 0)?) {

    let strongest = power[1..].iter().copied().fold(0.0, f64::max);
    if strongest <= 0.0 {

/// A power of two close to `max_abs`, the largest absolute value in some data, to divide
/// the data by. MUSIC does not depend on the data's scale, and dividing by a power of two
/// is exact, so this changes no result: it only keeps the sums of squares in the
/// covariance and energy from overflowing for very loud data (or underflowing for very
/// quiet data).
fn power_of_two_scale(max_abs: f64) -> f64 {
    if max_abs > 0.0 {
        2f64.powi((max_abs.log2().floor() as i32).clamp(-1000, 1000))
    } else {
        1.0
    }
}

/// `data` divided by [`power_of_two_scale`] of its largest absolute value.
fn normalised_real(data: &DMatrix<f64>) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    data / power_of_two_scale(data.amax())
}

/// The mean of `values`, summed with Neumaier's compensated summation so that it is
/// correct to about one ulp: subtracting it from constant data then leaves (almost)
/// nothing, which [`SILENCE_RATIO`] relies on. With a plain sum, 16000 samples of 0.3
/// leave a residue above the threshold.
fn accurate_mean<'a>(values: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a f64>) -> f64 {
    let n = values.len() as f64;
    let (mut sum, mut compensation) = (0.0_f64, 0.0_f64);
    for &x in values {
        let t = sum + x;
        compensation += if sum.abs() >= x.abs() {
            (sum - t) + x
        } else {
            (x - t) + sum
        };
        sum = t;
    }
    (sum + compensation) / n
}

    if !data.iter().all(|x| x.is_finite()) {
        return Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData);
    }
    Ok(())

type CVec = DVector<Cplx>;

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Hermitian eigendecomposition (pure nalgebra, no LAPACK)
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Eigendecomposition of a complex Hermitian n×n matrix using faer's dedicated
/// complex selfadjoint solver, which is numerically more stable than the real
/// block-matrix trick for near-degenerate noise subspaces.
///
/// Returns `(eigenvalues, eigenvectors)` sorted by ascending eigenvalue.
/// `eigenvalues[k]` is real; `eigenvectors.column(k)` is the unit-norm eigenvector.
fn hermitian_eigen(mat: &CMatrix) -> (Vec<f64>, CMatrix) {
    use faer::complex_native::c64;
    use faer::{Mat as FaerMat, Side};

    let n = mat.nrows();

    // Convert nalgebra complex matrix → faer complex matrix
    let faer_mat: FaerMat<c64> = FaerMat::from_fn(n, n, |i, j| {
        let c = mat[(i, j)];
        c64::new(c.re, c.im)
    });

    // Numerically stable Hermitian eigendecomposition
    // Note: faer does not guarantee a sort order, so we sort ascending afterward.
    let evd = faer_mat.selfadjoint_eigendecomposition(Side::Lower);

    // Eigenvalues are real but stored as c64 with im ≈ 0; extract via .re
    let s_col = evd.s().column_vector();
    let u_mat = evd.u();

    // Sort by ascending (real) eigenvalue
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();
    order.sort_unstable_by(|&a, &b| s_col.read(a).re.total_cmp(&s_col.read(b).re));

    let eigenvalues: Vec<f64> = order.iter().map(|&i| s_col.read(i).re).collect();
    // Copy the eigenvectors (reordered by ascending eigenvalue) back into nalgebra.
    // faer's eigenvectors already satisfy A·v = λ·v, so no conjugation is applied;
    // the steering-vector sign convention in `steering_vector` is matched to this.
    let eigenvectors: CMatrix = CMatrix::from_fn(n, n, |row, col| {
        let src_col = order[col];
        let c = u_mat.read(row, src_col);
        Cplx::new(c.re, c.im)
    });

    (eigenvalues, eigenvectors)
}

    EmptyData,
    /// The data is shorter than one STFT window, so it has no complete window.
    DataShorterThanWindow { nfft: usize, samples: usize },
    /// The data contains a NaN or infinite value.
    NonFiniteData,

    /// every selected frequency bin is: there is no signal to locate.
    SilentData,
    /// `n_sources` must be less than the number of antennas, so that a noise subspace
    /// is left.
    TooManySources { n_sources: usize, n_antennas: usize },
    /// The STFT window size `nfft` is 0.
    InvalidNfft,
    /// The STFT overlap must be less than the window size.

fn read_wav_4ch(path: &str) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    let mut reader = hound::WavReader::open(path).expect("failed to open WAV file");

    let raw: Vec<i32> = reader.samples::<i32>().map(Result::unwrap).collect();

}
